doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

chapter: Denver youth and University of Denver
title: University of Denver jazz band and State Department tour of Asia
summary: Ricker names All-State clarinet and the University of Denver as turning points; the jazz band won Notre Dame and toured Asia for three months in 1965. Jazz for credit was rare then.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you have, as a teenager, what I’ll call an aha moment? An epiphany of any sort that you remember that really directed your career path?

Well I always liked to practice and so my parents didn’t have to bug me about that. And there were a couple of things along the way. I got principal clarinet in the Colorado — I’m from Denver — so in the Colorado All-State and that was a big one, and it kind of moved me on, and I went to the University of Denver, I lived at home. It’s a good school and I had a good clarinet teacher and a good jazz band. In fact we were sent in 1965 to Asia, we were sent for three months on a State Department tour. And that was the result that we won the Notre Dame Jazz Festival the previous year. That’s when it was really a contest and the State Department people were there. And they, you know they liked the band, they also liked that the band was diverse and so yeah, three months touring Asia. It was a great, great trip.

Was the jazz group considered a part of the music department at that time? Because I know when I was at Fredonia in the late 60s we had a fine jazz group but it was mostly student-run and sometimes hard to get a space to perform in. They had an arm’s length sort of relationship with it.

Yeah, well yes this was, we got credit for it and it had an outside director. It wasn’t student run. And there weren’t many places in the U.S. or probably in the world at that time that they gave credit, and that was sort of a big deal. North Texas State was one and us, University of Denver, and then some of the big ten schools around that time, I remember Michigan State had a good band and they rehearsed as part of the curriculum. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
But really jazz education was in its infancy at that time and to play in the big band was just sort of the first step.
Yes. Were you one of the players that the director might be able to point to and say, “You got it, I need an improvised solo here”?
